from: July book, night 1 (Bread from the Ravens)
p1: Long ago, King Rehoboam would not listen to the wise old men. So his kingdom broke in two. One king made gold calves for people to pray to.
Later, many people stopped following the Lord. So Elijah told King Ahab, “No rain for years, until I say so.”
Then the Lord told Elijah to hide by a little stream called a brook. Elijah trusted the Lord and went.
p2: Every morning and every evening, big black birds called ravens came. They brought Elijah bread and meat! He drank water from the brook. The Lord took care of Elijah.
The Lord takes care of you too. Tonight, think of one food you ate today. Say thank you to Heavenly Father for it.
old: Elijah was a prophet who loved Heavenly Father. He told the wicked king there would be no rain for a long time. Then Heavenly Father said, “Go hide by the little brook. I will take care of you.”
Elijah went and stayed by the brook. He drank the cool, clear water. But where would he get food? There were no stores out there.
Then something amazing happened! Big black birds called ravens flew to Elijah. They carried bread and meat in their beaks. They brought him food every morning and every night.

Heavenly Father took care of Elijah in a surprising way. He uses all sorts of helpers — even birds! When we trust Him, He always finds a way to take care of us. Heavenly Father never forgets His children.
